__schema__: Per-class in-class actions. Keyed by a class's class_id (see schedule.json). Each class lists `events`; each event is one thing the PLAYER can do while that class is in session, and replaces the generic Focus/Socialize/Daydream verbs for the player (NPCs still use the generic verbs). Fields: id (unique), name (button label), learn ('focus' | 'attend' — drives how much of the class's stat it grants), effects (optional, applied on take), descriptions (ordered variants; the FIRST whose optional `requires` is met is shown in the journal, so put specific / higher-level variants first and a plain default with no `requires` last). `requires` uses the same shape as everything else (min_stats/tags/without_tags/flags/…), so a description can branch on ANY stat — e.g. how a mana exercise reads depending on your shaping level.

descriptions.text: You work through the assigned case, testing each precedent against the next until the reasoning holds.
You follow the arguments loosely, catching the shape of the law if not every detail.
Shaping has taught your hands the feel of live mana, so when the class reaches for the ambient flow you find it almost at once — and spend the hour refining rather than searching.
You have shaped enough to know the mana is really there; you catch the edge of the current and lose it, over and over, but each near-miss teaches you a little.
The others murmur about 'feeling the flow' and you feel nothing at all — only the cold of the hall and your own frustration. You copy the motions and hope the sense comes later.
You let the lecture wash over you, noting what you can of the diagrams of flow and reserve.
You trace the dynasties and their wars, fixing the order of it in your memory.
You half-listen, letting the old names drift past like a story told at a fire.
You push through the conditioning drills, forcing yourself to read every feint and tell before it lands.
You go through the motions of the drill, breaking a light sweat but saving your strength.
You bend a thread of raw mana into the set shape, over and over, until your hands stop shaking.
You watch the demonstration and copy it loosely, more spectator than shaper.
You wrestle with the first principles of sorcery, filling the margins of your notes with questions.
You skim along the surface of the theory, catching the gist and little else.
